question.text: Arbitrage in the derivatives market involves:

answer.text: Exploiting price differentials between the cash and derivatives markets for riskless profits
Taking a long position expecting prices to rise
Using derivatives to protect an existing portfolio from losses
Writing options to earn premium income

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 198, arbitrage means buying in the cheaper market and selling in the costlier market to capture riskless profits. Per page 211, this is applied to derivative-market price differences after accounting for borrowing cost. Page 177 supports the cash-vs-derivatives price-differential idea in the arbitrage-fund context. The Trap: Taking a long position on a directional view is speculation. Using derivatives to protect a portfolio is hedging. Writing options for premium is an income strategy, not the arbitrage mechanic described in the source. Note: The defining feature of arbitrage in the source is the simultaneous offsetting position in two markets to lock in a price differential.
